role: WindowSelector configuration and selection logic: 30-70% sleep band resolution (wall-clock to t_ms translation), two-pass artifact scanning, organized-window ranking (Tier 1 score or RMSSD), peak-capacity scan, peak-metric and manual window selection, zone merging, adaptive window sizing.
types: WindowSelector.Config: struct — window size 400, step 40, artifact limits 0.10/0.15, minCleanBeats 300, ectopic 20%/10-beat median, band 0.30-0.70, stabilityWeight 10, isolatedSpikeRatio 1.5
WindowSelector.SleepBoundaries: struct — recording and sleep boundaries
WindowSelector.SearchBand: struct — index range and ms limits of the band
toplevel: Config property defaults (S:12-76) set every selector threshold; Config.default = Config().

flags.text: SleepBoundaries mixes coordinate origins: recordingStartMs/EndMs are absolute first/last t_ms, while actualSleepStartMs/EndMs and recordingDurationMs are 0-based offsets from the first beat (tMsOffset returns match.t_ms - first.t_ms). findSearchBand adds band fractions to the offsets and compares them with absolute t_ms, and scoredBlock's relative position mixes the same; correct only when the first beat's t_ms is 0 (true for the decoders, not guaranteed for merged/rebased series, e.g. DataSourceSelector rebases gap-fill t_ms to wallClockMs).

logWindowRanking writes raw per-window values (tier1=, meanHR=, cv=, pos=) to debugLog while logSelectedWindow deliberately redacts the same metrics; DebugLogger.scrubPHI's metric pattern needs a word boundary before 'HR' and has no 'tier1'/'cv' key, so 'meanHR=58' and 'tier1=82.3' land unredacted in the user-exportable log when persistent logging is enabled.

units.does: Main automatic selector: resolves the 30-70% sleep band (clearing lastOrganizedZones), scans it with the strict-then-permissive artifact passes, and returns the best organized window (Tier 1 ranked with a baseline, else RMSSD) or nil; populates lastOrganizedZones as a side effect.

branches.cond: searchBand returns nil (<120 beats, no points, or empty band)
no windows survive either artifact pass
branches.effect: return nil; else select organized window

units.does: Clears lastOrganizedZones, requires >=120 beats, resolves sleep boundaries, logs, finds the 30-70% search band, logs it, and returns (boundaries, band) or nil.

branches.effect: log 'No points' and return nil (unreachable after the 120-beat guard)
log and return nil; else log band and return

units.does: Scans the band at the strict 10% artifact limit; only if that yields zero windows rescans at 15%; returns the windows (empty if both passes find none).

branches.effect: use strict windows; else rescan at config.maxArtifactRate 0.15

branches.cond: fell back and permissive pass found windows

branches.effect: log and return []; else return windows

units.does: Applies filterIsolatedSpikes to the windows and logs how many were rejected; returns the kept windows.

branches.effect: log rejection count; else nothing extra

units.does: Spike-filters the windows, keeps only isOrganizedRecovery ones, stores their merged time ranges in lastOrganizedZones, and builds the recovery window from them; nil when none are organized.

branches.effect: log and return nil (peak fallback happens in caller); else buildRecoveryWindow

flags.text: filterIsolatedSpikes never rejects the first or last window, so a non-empty input always yields a non-empty output; the 'filteredWindows.isEmpty ? allWindows' fallback cannot fire (findBestWindow already returned on empty). Same at findPeakMetricWindow:603.

units.does: Writes the merged start/end ranges of the organized windows into lastOrganizedZones.
Logs which sleep-start/wake boundaries were used and the recording/sleep spans.

branches.effect: log offset; else log 'using recording start'

branches.cond: wake present and after sleep start
branches.effect: log either capped (229) or HealthKit wake; else log 'using recording end'
log capping; else log the wake offset

flags.text: Logs compare the raw wall-clock sleepStartMs/wakeTimeMs to recordingDurationMs, while resolveSleepBoundaries actually translates them through wallClockMs; on nights with BLE dropouts the logged decision (capped or not) can differ from what was used.

units.does: Logs the band limits, band duration/beats and adaptive window size for diagnostics.
Scans the band with the adaptive window/step size using sleep start/end as the relative-position span and the given artifact limit.
Ranks organized windows (Tier 1 score vs baseline when baselineStats given, else RMSSD) and builds the RecoveryWindow from the top one; nil for an empty list.

branches.effect: rank by Tier 1 score; nil baseline uses rankByRMSSD
return nil; else build from first

units.does: Scores each organized window with RecoveryScoreCalculator.calculateTier1 (rmssd, meanHR, a1, baseline, no readiness), logs the ranking, and sorts by score, then RMSSD, then later relative position.

branches.effect: higher RMSSD first; else later relativePosition first

units.does: Logs one multi-line ranking entry with each window's Tier 1 score, RMSSD, SDNN, mean HR, a1, LF/HF, CV, position and start minute.

flags.text: Writes meanHR, tier1 score and CV values that the PHI scrubber does not match (see file flag), unlike logSelectedWindow which redacts.

units.does: Sorts organized windows by RMSSD descending, ties to later relative position, and logs the no-baseline fallback.

branches.effect: higher first; else later position first

units.does: Builds the RecoveryWindow from the chosen block: isConsolidated = block present in sustainedWindows and HR CV < 0.08, qualityScore = RMSSD/100, recoveryScore with stability weight, isOrganizedRecovery true, classification from the block.

flags.text: isSustained is always true (organized windows are drawn from filteredWindows, which is non-empty whenever there are windows) and every organized block already has HR CV < 0.08 (isOrganizedRecovery requires hrIsStable when lfHfRatio is nil, always in production), so isConsolidated is always true for this path.

units.does: Formats the stored selection reason 'Organized Recovery (RMSSD x ms, a1=y, CV z%) at p%'.
Logs the selected window (values redacted), warning when its position lies outside the configured band.

branches.effect: log warning with timestamps; else no warning

units.does: Sorts time ranges by start and merges ranges that overlap or touch into contiguous zones.

branches.effect: extend the last merged zone; else append as new zone

units.does: Combined entry used by the analysis pipeline: requires >= beatsPerWindow (400) beats, gets an organized recovery window or the peak-RMSSD fallback, computes peak capacity across the whole recording, and returns both (nil only when neither exists).

branches.effect: return nil if recovery window also nil, else result with peakCapacity nil

flags.text: baselineStats defaults to nil, so callers that omit it silently switch ranking from Tier 1 score to raw RMSSD; RRCollector+DeviceRecording:186 omits it while HRVAnalysisPipeline/SessionRecoveryService/ReanalysisService pass one, so device-recording results can pick a different window than morning processing for the same night (ReanalysisService:210 documents this exact divergence as a past bug).

Docs say the recovery window is nil when no organized recovery occurred ('If no organized recovery occurred, recoveryWindow will be nil'; WindowSelectionResult.recoveryWindow 'nil if no organized recovery detected'), but recoveryOrPeakFallback returns the peak-RMSSD window from the band in that case, so recoveryWindow is non-nil and hasConsolidatedRecovery (recoveryWindow != nil) would report consolidated recovery for an unorganized fallback window.

units.does: Returns findBestWindow's organized window when there is one, else the peak-RMSSD window in the same band.

branches.effect: log and return it; else fall back to peakRMSSDFallback

units.does: Runs findPeakMetricWindow(.rmssd) in the 30-70% band and logs whether a window was found.

branches.effect: log success; else log 'will analyze full session'

units.does: Scans the entire recording with the compact adaptive window, spike-filters, and returns PeakCapacity from the highest-RMSSD sustained window (relative position against recording span); nil for an empty series or no windows.
Maps the peak block to PeakCapacity (RMSSD, SDNN, totalPower nil, duration minutes, relative position, mean HR).
Logs the peak-capacity scan's recording length, beat count, BPM and window size.
Dispatches by WindowSelectionMethod: consolidatedRecovery → findBestWindow (no baseline), peak methods → findPeakMetricWindow with the metric, custom → nil.

flags.text: The .consolidatedRecovery case is never reached in production: the only production caller, ReanalysisService.selectWindow, returns before calling it for that method, and tests only pass .peakRMSSD. Its comment promises Tier 1 ranking 'when a baseline exists' but the function takes no baseline, so it would always rank by RMSSD.

units.does: Selects the window with the highest RMSSD or SDNN in the 30-70% band (strict-then-permissive artifact passes, spike filter), regardless of organization, and builds a RecoveryWindow.

branches.effect: use all windows (unreachable: edges never removed)
log and return nil (unreachable with non-empty candidates); else build window

units.does: Same as searchBand but without clearing lastOrganizedZones or logging boundaries: >=120 beats, resolve boundaries, find band.

branches.effect: log and return nil (unreachable after count guard)
log and return nil; else return

flags.text: Near-copy of searchBand (S:105) differing only in skipping the zone reset and logging; the 120 literal duplicates minRequiredBeats.

units.does: Two-pass strict(10%) then permissive(15%) band scan for peak selection; returns [] and logs when both are empty.

branches.effect: rescan at 15%; else use strict windows

flags.text: Duplicates scanBandWithArtifactFallback (S:145) minus its fallback log line.

units.does: Logs the peak-selection band duration, beats and adaptive window size.
Returns the candidate with max RMSSD for .rmssd, else max SDNN (logging that total power is approximated by SDNN).

flags.text: WindowSelectionMethod.peakTotalPower ('highest total spectral power') never computes spectral power; it selects by SDNN, so it is identical to peakSDNN except for the reason label.

units.does: Builds a RecoveryWindow for a peak-selected block, carrying its real isOrganizedRecovery and isConsolidated = organized && CV < 0.08.

flags.text: windowClassification comes from ScoredRecoveryBlock.classification, which labels any a1 in 0.75-1.0 (or no a1 with CV<8%) 'Organized Recovery' even when HR CV >= 8% makes isOrganizedRecovery false; a peak/manual window can be stored with isOrganizedRecovery=false yet classification 'Organized Recovery', which MorningResultsView shows as 'Organized'.

units.does: Formats 'Peak <metric> (value ms, a1, CV%) at p%' and logs the selection.
Returns the metric name and formatted value: RMSSD, SDNN, or 'SDNN (Total Power proxy)' with the SDNN value.

User 'Pick Window' path: requires >=400 beats, centres a 400-beat window on the first beat at/after targetMs (pulled back at recording end), evaluates it with the artifact gate disabled (limit 1.0) and returns the manual RecoveryWindow; nil when too short, target past the end, or too little signal.

branches.effect: return nil; else build manual window

flags.text: No test calls analyzeAtPosition, the user-facing manual window override.

units.does: Finds the first beat with t_ms >= targetMs, centres a beatsPerWindow window on it and shifts it back to fit when it would overrun the end.

branches.effect: log 'outside recording range' and return nil
clamp end to count and start to max(0, end-400); else keep centred window

flags.text: Comment says 'closest to target time' but it takes the first beat at or after it, and a tap past the last beat's t_ms returns nil (UI does nothing) instead of selecting the last window.

units.does: Evaluates the manual window with artifactRateLimit 1.0 so only the >=50 valid RR and clean-beat guards can reject it; logs and returns nil on rejection.

branches.effect: log 'too little usable signal' and return nil; else return block

units.does: Builds the manual RecoveryWindow carrying the block's isOrganizedRecovery and isConsolidated = organized && CV < 0.08.
Formats 'Manual selection at p% (RMSSD, a1, CV%)'.
actualSleepEndMs - actualSleepStartMs.
endExclusive - startIdx.

Resolves recording start/end (absolute first/last t_ms) and sleep start/end as 0-based t_ms offsets: sleep start translated from wall-clock via tMsOffset (0 when absent), sleep end from wake via sleepEndOffset.

branches.effect: sleep start 0 (recording start); else max(0, translated offset)

units.does: Translated wake offset clamped to the recording duration when it lies after sleep start; otherwise the recording duration.

Maps a wall-clock offset to a t_ms offset from the first beat by finding the first beat whose wallClockMs >= firstWall + offset; identity when the series has no wall clock; recording span when the target is past the last beat.

branches.cond: a beat with wallClockMs >= target exists

branches.effect: return last t_ms - first t_ms (falls back to first t_ms, i.e. 0, if last were nil)

flags.text: Doc says the input is 'ms from session start' but the target is computed as firstWall + offset, i.e. relative to the first beat's wall clock; when the first beat arrives W0 ms after session start the boundaries shift later by W0. Beats with nil wallClockMs mid-series are treated as Int64.min and skipped.

units.does: Computes the 30%-70% points of the sleep span, clamps them to the recording, and returns the index range of beats inside, or nil when empty.

branches.cond: a start index and end index exist with end >= start

units.does: Window size: beatsPerWindow when enough beats; otherwise half (band) or a third (compact) of the beats when >= 240/360 beats, else max(60, 60%/40%); step = max(10, size/10).

branches.effect: beats/3 if >= 360 else max(60, 2/5 of beats)
